judge.shardDecision: Read in full by the judge, no shard dispatched. The bundle is 1338 lines across three files and the four member-answerable families (currency, conventions, self-sufficiency, testability) all turn on the same small set of facts — the two country columns, one capability, one shipped member route and one shipped holidays gate — so splitting it would have made three readers re-establish the same facts and would have hidden the two findings that only appear when the behaviour file, the contracts file and the mock are held together (the MemberCapability contradiction, and the band tokens the mock defines but no DS-gaps row records). Verification was done directly against the code instead: schema, roles.ts, MemberCapability, members.service.ts, holidays.service.ts, reports.service.ts, the ds barrel and token files, the e2e helper line numbers.

judge.shardDecision: Read in full by the judge, no shard dispatched. `spec-slice --since df2e3aa` reported the bundle unchanged and offered that as the finding, which is wrong and is why nothing was delegated: df2e3aa *is* the repair commit, so `df2e3aa..HEAD` excludes the very diff this pass exists to judge. The change under judgement is therefore `git show df2e3aa` — 155 changed lines across the three bundle files, plus an uncommitted repair to specs/time-off/README.md — a slice small enough that splitting it would have cost three readers the same re-establishment of the same five facts (the two capability unions and their two helpers, the holidays gates' status shapes, the member route's refusal statuses, the four absent DS tokens, the timezone column's nullability). Both blockers below are also invisible to a per-member split: each is a disagreement between the repaired line in one file and a line the repair did not touch in another.

keys: spec/incomplete-decision:Roles & Permission Matrix — the Decided that settled R1, against REQ-01-003 and the matrix

request: A vacation calendar based on holidays and vacation requests, viewable for the whole organization, for several teams, or for specific people, drawn as a horizontal timeline where each row is a member and each column is a day. Holidays follow a country a manager states on the member, falling back to a country stated on the organization; the phone country code is not a source.
